COUNTY OF SAN DIEGO BOARD OF SUPERVISORS
  REGULAR MEETING
  MEETING AGENDA
  TUESDAY, OCTOBER 6, 2026, 9:00 AM
  COUNTY ADMINISTRATION CENTER
  BOARD CHAMBER, ROOM 327
  1600 PACIFIC HIGHWAY
  SAN DIEGO, CA 92101
County of San Diego Board of Supervisors
General Legislative Session
Tuesday, October 6, 2026, 9:00 a.m.

A.  Roll Call

B.  Opening Ceremonial Matters
  1) Invocation
  2) Pledge of Allegiance
  3) Presentation or Announcement of Proclamations and Awards

C.  Non-Agenda Public Comment
  Individuals can address the Board on topics within its jurisdiction that are not on the agenda.
  According to the Board’s Rules of Procedure, each person may speak at only one Non-Agenda
  Public Comment session per meeting. Speakers can choose to speak during either the General
  Legislative or Land Use Legislative Session.

D.  Approval of Statements of Proceedings/Minutes
  Approval of the Statement of Proceedings/Minutes for the sessions of September 15, 2026, and
  September 16, 2026.

E.  Consent Agenda
  All agenda items listed under this section are considered to be routine and will be acted
  upon with one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a member
  of the Board of Supervisors or the Chief Administrative Officer so requests, in which
  event, the item will be considered separately in its normal sequence.

Tuesday, October 6, 2026  1
 1.  Sheriff - Continuation of Current Vehicle Registration Fee to Fund California
  Identification System Fingerprint Equipment and Services (Districts: All)

  Recommendation by Sheriff:
  1) Adopt a resolution entitled: A RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF SUPERVISORS OF
  THE COUNTY OF SAN DIEGO AUTHORIZING THE CONTINUATION OF THE VEHICLE
  REGISTRATION FEE TO FUND CALIFORNIA IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM
  FINGERPRINT EQUIPMENT AND SERVICES.

  2) Waive Board Policy B-29, Fees, Grants, and Revenue Contracts - Department Responsibility
  for Cost Recovery which requires full cost recovery.
  Attachments: Board Letter
  Agenda Information Sheet
  Approval Log
  Attachment A - Resolution
  Attachment B - Summary of Proposed Resolution

2.  Authorize Extension to Contract 572191 with Traditions Behavioral Health for Medical
  Services Group Services (Districts: All)

  Recommendation by Chief Administrative Officer:
  In accordance with Board Policy A-87, Competitive Procurement, and Administrative Code
  Section 401, authorize the Director, Department of Purchasing and Contracting, to amend
  contract 572191 with Traditions Behavioral Health, for medical service group services, by
  extending the contract for one seven-month option and two one-year option periods through June
  30, 2029, and to amend the agreement as required to reflect changes to services or funding
  allocation, subject to the approval of the Director of Behavioral Health Services.
  Attachments: Board Letter
  Agenda Information Sheet
  Approval Log

3.  Authorize Competitive Solicitation for Visitation, Transportation and Family Visit
  Coaching Services (Districts: All)

  Recommendation by Chief Administrative Officer:
  In accordance with Section 401, Article XXIII of the County Administrative Code, authorize the
  Director, Department of Purchasing and Contracting, to issue a Competitive Solicitation for the
  Visitation, Transportation, and Family Visit Coaching services, and upon successful negotiations
  and determination of a fair and reasonable price, award a contract for the period of up to one

Tuesday, October 6, 2026  2
   year and up to four option years, and up to six additional months if needed, subject to the
  availability of funds; and to amend the contract(s) as required to reflect changes in services and
  funding allocations, subject to the approval of the Deputy Chief Administrative Officer, Health
  and Human Services Agency.
  Attachments: Board Letter
  Agenda Information Sheet
  Approval Log

4.  Authorize Competitive Solicitation for Community Services for Families Program
  (Districts: All)

  Recommendation by Chief Administrative Officer:
  In accordance with Section 401, Article XXIII of the County Administrative Code, authorize the
  Director, Department of Purchasing and Contracting, to issue a Competitive Solicitation for the
  Community Services for Families program, and upon successful negotiations and determination
  of a fair and reasonable price, award a contract(s) for the period of up to one year and up to four
  option years, and up to six additional months if needed, subject to the availability of funds; and
  to amend the contract(s) as required to reflect changes in services and funding allocations,
  subject to the approval of the Deputy Chief Administrative Officer, Health and Human Services
  Agency.
  Attachments: Board Letter
  Agenda Information Sheet
  Approval Log

5.  Authorize Renewal Agreement with the California Franchise Tax Board for the Collection
  of Court-Ordered Debt (Districts: All)

  Recommendation by Chief Administrative Officer:
  1) Authorize the Assistant Chief Administrative Officer/Chief Financial Officer to execute
  a renewal agreement with the California Franchise Tax Board (FTB) for continued
  participation in the Court-Ordered Debt Collection Program and any extensions in the
  future so long as the fee charged by the FTB does not exceed maximum permitted by
  law.
  2) Authorize the Auditor and Controller, Office of Revenue and Recovery to continue
  referring eligible delinquent court-ordered debt to the FTB for collection services
  Attachments: Board Letter
  Agenda Information Sheet
  Approval Log
  Attachment A - Client Communication Letter

Tuesday, October 6, 2026  3

  Planning Groups and Post Vacancies (Districts: All)

  Recommendation by Chief Administrative Officer:
  1) Appoint the nominees to designated positions in the specific special districts and community
  planning groups in which there are candidates, but the number of candidates equals or is less
  than the number of positions to be filled (Attachment A, on file with the Clerk of the Board).

  2) Accept the list of vacancies requiring appointments and direct the Clerk of the Board to post

  Attachments: Board Letter

8.  Appointments to Boards, Commissions, and Committees (Districts: All)

  Recommendation by Chair Terra Lawson-Remer:
  1) Appoint Missy Bell to Child And Family Strengthening Advisory Board of San Diego,
  Seat 23, to complete the unexpired term, set to expire February 06, 2028.
  2) Appoint Sam McMannus to fill Seat 4 on the Jacumba Community Services District
  Board, currently vacant, and to complete the unexpired term for Seat 4, set to expire on
  December 4, 2026.

Tuesday, October 6, 2026  5
 F.  Discussion Items
  These items are presented for Board consideration and public discussion. Discussion Items
  may involve staff presentations and deliberation by the Board. The Board may provide
  direction, adopt recommendations, or take other appropriate actions. Please note that the
  Board may take items in a different order than they appear on the agenda.

10.  Receive a Presentation on the County of San Diego’s El Niño and Severe Weather
  Preparedness Actions Taken to Strengthen Community Preparedness, and Approve
  Amendments to and Sunset Date for Board Policy K-011, and Ratify a Proclamation of
  Local Emergency (Districts: All)

  Recommendation by Chief Administrative Officer:
  1) Receive a presentation on the County of San Diego's El Niño and severe weather preparedness
  efforts in response to the Board of Supervisor's September 15, 2026 (20), direction.

  2) Approve amendments to and the sunset review date of December 31, 2033, for Board of
  Supervisors Policy K-011, Use and Distribution of County-Owned Sandbags and Other
  Resources.

  3) Ratify the PROCLAMATION OF THE EXISTENCE OF A COUNTY-WIDE LOCAL
  EMERGENCY (UNINCORPORATED AND INCORPORATED AREAS OF SAN DIEGO
  COUNTY) FOR THE PLANNING AND PREPARATION FOR EQUITABLE RESPONSE TO,
  AND RECOVERY FROM ANTICIPATED IMPACTS FROM THE DEVELOPING 2026-2027
  EL NIÑO, WITH PARTICULAR ATTENTION TO VULNERABLE AND UNDERSERVED
  COMMUNITIES made by the Chief Administrative Officer of the County of San Diego as
  Director of Emergency Services on September 30, 2026 (Attachment F, on file with the Clerk of
  the Board of Supervisors).

  4) Find that there is a need for continuing the local emergency until no longer needed, subject to
  Government Code 8630 review requirements.

  5) Direct the Chief Administrative Officer to allocate and use up to $1,000,000 within the
  Unlocked Reserves Framework in Finance Other to support emergent needs to protect the health,
  safety, and wellbeing of County residents in response to a natural disaster, including wildfires,
  floods, or other severe weather events such as El Niño.

Tuesday, October 6, 2026  6

  Attachment E - K-011 Clean

11.  Protecting Youth With California’s Largest Regional E-Bike Injury Warning System
  (Districts: All)

  Recommendation by Supervisor Terra Lawson-Remer and Supervisor Paloma Aguirre
  1) Direct the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO) to establish a Regional E-Bike Injury
  Warning System to collect, aggregate, and publicly report regional e-bike injury data on
  an ongoing basis using currently available data.
  2) As a subsequent part of this initiative, the CAO should coordinate with hospitals, trauma
  centers, emergency departments, community clinics, EMS providers, and other regional
  healthcare and law enforcement partners, as appropriate, to monitor emerging injury
  trends, deliberate data quality improvement efforts, and discuss additional potential data
  sources and sharing that may be beneficial to collect, aggregate, and publicly report of
  the Regional E-Bike Injury Warning System.
  Attachments: Board Letter
  Agenda Information Sheet

12.  Improve Fairness, Civility, Accessibility, and Efficiency at Board Meetings: Amending
  Rules for Public Participation (Districts: All)

  Recommendation by Chair Terra Lawson-Remer:
  Adopt the proposed resolution entitled RESOLUTION AMENDING MEETING
  MANAGEMENT RULES IN THE RULES OF PROCEDURE OF THE SAN DIEGO
  COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS
  Attachments: Board Letter
  Agenda Information Sheet
  Attachment A - Resolution
  Attachment B - Exhibit A

Tuesday, October 6, 2026  7
 13.  Strengthening Accountability and Transparency by Establishing a Five-Year Minimum
  Retention Requirement for County Public Records and Communications (Districts: All)

  Recommendations by Supervisor Joel Anderson
  Direct the Chief Administrative Officer to return to the Board within 120 days with
  recommendations and options to update County retention standards, including establishing a
  minimum five-year retention requirement for County records and communications, including
  emails and text messages, and include the estimated cost, potential funding source(s), and other
  considerations to implement each identified option.
  Attachments: Board Letter
  Agenda Information Sheet

14.  Receive Presentation and Provide Direction on the San Diego County Film Initiative
  Implementation Plan (Districts: All)

  Recommendation by Chief Administrative Officer:
  1) Receive a presentation on the San Diego County Film Initiative Implementation Plan.
  2) Receive options for operationalizing the San Diego County Film Initiative Implementation
  Plan and select one of the following options:

  a) Option A Nonprofit Model: Direct the Chief Administrative Officer to
  operationalize the San Diego County Film Initiative Implementation Plan based
  on the proposed Nonprofit Model and return back in 90 days with an ordinance
  formalizing the County’s role in the Film Initiative and an update on the
  development of the Film Office Nonprofit and Film Commission.
  OR
  b) Option B In-House Model: Direct the Chief Administrative Officer to
  operationalize the San Diego County Film Initiative Implementation Plan based on the
  proposed In-House Model and return back in 90 days with an ordinance formalizing the
  County’s role in the Film Initiative and an update on the development of the Film Office
  County Unit and Film Commission.
  Attachments: Board Letter
  Agenda Information Sheet
  Approval Log
  Attachment A - Implementation Plan

15.  Oppose the Placement of Sexually Violent Predators Michael Poulsom and Reynaldo
  Delrosario in the Unincorporated Community of Boulevard and Waive Board Policy A-72
  (Districts: All)

Tuesday, October 6, 2026  8
   Recommendations by Supervisor Joel Anderson and Supervisor Jim Desmond
  1) Waive Board Policy A-72 Agenda and Related Process, Section 2.C.2.ii, which
  establishes required timelines for review when preparing a Board Letter.

  2) Direct the Chief Administrative Officer to send a letter to San Diego Superior Court
  Judge Theodore Weathers informing him of the recent escape of Sexually Violent
  Predator Merle Wakefield and requesting that Judge Weathers reject the release of
  Sexually Violent Predators Michael Poulsom and Reynaldo Delrosario from the
  Department of State Hospitals (DSH) and the placement of these two Sexually Violent
  Predators in the unincorporated community of Boulevard.

  3) Direct the Chief Administrative Officer to send a letter to the Department of State
  Hospitals and their contractor, Liberty Healthcare, asking them to inform the County of
  the actions they are taking to locate and return Sexually Violent Predator Merle
  Wakefield into their guardianship and asking them to inform the County of the actions
  they will take to ensure that the other Sexually Violent Predators they are monitoring in
  San Diego County will not evade the monitoring conditions of their parole.
  Attachments: Board Letter
  Agenda Information Sheet
  Attachment A
  Late Docket Request Memo

16.  Closed Session (Districts: All)

  Recommendation by Chief Administrative Officer:
  At the direction of the Board.
  Attachments: Board Letter
  Agenda Information Sheet

G.  Special Districts
  When the Board of Supervisors meets as the governing body of a special district, they are
  acting in a different capacity than during their regular County business. In this role, the
  Board makes decisions that apply only to that specific district, such as approving its
  budgets, projects, policies, and operations. These actions are legally separate from the
  Board’s actions as the County of San Diego, and they apply only to the area and
  responsibilities of the special district.

Special Districts Consent Agenda
None

Special Districts Discussion Items
None

Tuesday, October 6, 2026  9
 H.  Closing Reports and Recess
  1) Board Member Committee Updates: This is an opportunity for Members of the Board
  to provide informational updates on their committee assignments. No action may be taken.

  2) Recess to Wednesday, October 7, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. for the Land Use Legislative Session

A.  REGULAR SESSION: Meeting was called to order at 9:06 a.m.

  PRESENT: Supervisors Terra Lawson-Remer, Chair; Monica Montgomery Steppe, Vice-Chair;
  Paloma Aguirre, Chair Pro Tem; Joel Anderson; Jim Desmond; also, Andrew Potter, Clerk of the
  Board of Supervisors.

B.  Invocation was led by Reverend Scott Santarosa, S.J. from the Our Lady of Guadalupe Parish.

  Pledge of Allegiance was led by Dr. Chandra Richards.

  Presentations or Announcement of Proclamations and Awards:

  Chair Terra Lawson-Remer presented a proclamation declaring the Week of October 1-8, 2026,
  to be San Diego Climate Change Week throughout the County of San Diego.

  Vice-Chair Monica Montgomery Steppe and Chair Pro Tem Paloma Aguirre presented a
  proclamation declaring the Month of October 2026, to be Filipino-American History Month
  throughout the County of San Diego.

  Chair Pro Tem Paloma Aguirre presented a proclamation declaring October 6, 2026, to be
  Frankie “Frankie V” Vinci Day throughout the County of San Diego.

  Supervisor Jim Desmond presented a proclamation declaring the Week of October 4-10, 2026, to
  be National 4-H Week throughout the County of San Diego.

  Cradle “Wave of Light” Day throughout the County of San Diego.

   ACTION:
  ON MOTION of Supervisor Aguirre, seconded by Supervisor Anderson, the Board of
  Supervisors took the following actions:

  1. Received a presentation on the San Diego County Film Initiative Implementation Plan.
  2. Selected Option A Nonprofit Model: Direct the Chief Administrative Officer to operationalize
  the San Diego County Film Initiative Implementation Plan based on the proposed Nonprofit
  Model and return back in 90 days with an ordinance formalizing the County’s role in the Film
  Initiative and an update on the development of the Film Office Nonprofit and Film Commission.
  3. Directed the Chief Administrative Officer, as part of the ordinance returning in 90 days, to
  include revisions to the governance structure of the Film Commission establishing a
  fifteen-member (15) body composed as follows, and include recommendations on qualifications
  and terms for the seats and how rotating members will be selected:
  a. Five (5) seats, one for each of the five Supervisorial Districts.
  b. Six (6) seats reserved for regional governmental and sovereign entities, including one seat for
  the City of San Diego, one seat for the Port of San Diego, and one seat for a federally recognized
  Tribal Nation within the County. The remaining three seats shall be geographically designated
  seats, with one seat each for South County, North County, and East County, rotating among the
  cities within each respective subregion, excluding the City of San Diego.
  c. Four (4) industry and community seats, representing sectors such as labor, production,
  education, arts, business, and tourism.
  4. Directed the Chief Administrative Officer to incorporate the governance changes outlined in
  Recommendation 3 into the Film Commission bylaws, appointment processes, and all related
  governance documents as part of the development of the Film Office and Film Commission
  under the selected model.
